title: ROAX type map v1
description: Binds record paths to ROAX type tags. This file is the schema FOR the type map; the type map itself does not exist yet (spec section 4.3) and building it is on the critical path. The type map is NORMATIVE data: two libraries carrying different type maps produce different roots for the same record, which is the highest-risk surface in the design (spec section 4). It is versioned with the specification and is part of the conformance corpus (docs/conformance-corpus.md class 11).

typeMapVersion.description: Version of this type map. ADDING an entry MUST bump it; CHANGING one is forbidden, and the difference is normative rather than stylistic. STATED LIMIT: both halves of that rule compare THIS file against an EARLIER version of it, and no JSON Schema keyword can see a second document, so the pattern below constrains the identifier's form and nothing more. The type-map build owns the comparison, and conformance class 11 owns the consequence, which is that a retagged path changes the root of every already-issued record reaching it. Adding a binding for a path the map does not yet cover is the normal case and is what makes fail-closed workable for an open-world profile like PDT. Retagging a path the map ALREADY covers changes the root of every already-issued record that reaches that path, which spec section 12.2 forbids, so a correction to an existing binding is a new PROFILE version rather than a type-map patch, and records anchored under the old binding keep verifying under it. An earlier version of this description said only that changing any entry must bump the version, which permitted the retag and asked only for a version bump; decision D7's ruling to D7a made the additive constraint explicit (spec section 4.2). A root computed under one type-map version is not reproducible under another if the changed entry was reachable, which is why the distinction matters at all. The three-part semver pattern is KEPT here on purpose, and the distinction is the one spec section 12.1 draws: this is one of ROAX's OWN artifacts, so this project defines the identifier and may legitimately constrain its shape. schemaVersion above is defined elsewhere - by the profile, and beyond it by FHIR or a health authority - and is therefore opaque. Do not 'harmonize' the two; they differ because their owners differ.

recordType.description: The profile this map applies to. Matches the envelope's recordType, and the reverse-DNS pattern is repeated here from schemas/envelope-1.0.json so that 'matches' is enforced at the level of FORM rather than only asserted. THE TWO PATTERNS MUST STAY IDENTICAL, for the reason the schemaVersion description below gives: recordType and schemaVersion together are the type-map lookup key, so a value this file rejects and the envelope accepts would make a valid record unable to find its own type map, which is the silent-divergence failure fail-closed exists to prevent. STATED LIMIT ON THAT MUST, because it is a claim about two files and no keyword in either can see the other: NOTHING AUTOMATED CHECKS IT. There is no CI and no build step that loads both schemas (AGENTS.md), so this is a review-time obligation on whoever edits either pattern, recorded here so a reader can tell it is unchecked rather than assume it is enforced. SEPARATE STATED LIMIT: form is all a pattern can check. Whether a syntactically valid value NAMES a real profile is settled by the registry in docs/profiles/, exactly as the envelope records for its own copy of this field (spec section 10.2).

schemaVersion.description: The profile version this map applies to. OPAQUE TO THE PROTOCOL, exactly as in the envelope, and deliberately carrying no dotted-numeric pattern: the value is never parsed, ordered or range-compared, only matched for equality against the profile registry (spec section 12.1). THIS CONSTRAINT MUST STAY IDENTICAL TO THE ENVELOPE'S. The two fields together form the type-map lookup key, so tightening one alone would make a record that validates as an envelope fail to find its own type map, which is the silent-divergence failure the fail-closed rule exists to prevent. STATED LIMIT, the same one recorded on recordType above: that MUST spans two files, nothing automated checks it because there is no CI and no build step that loads both schemas (AGENTS.md), and it is therefore a review-time obligation rather than a machine-checked one.

sourceSchemas.description: Provenance: which reference schemas this map was derived from, cited by path and commit. The reference schemata live OUTSIDE this repository by design and are never copied in.

entries.description: Path-pattern to type-tag bindings. Order is significant: the FIRST matching entry wins, so more specific patterns MUST precede more general ones. STATED LIMIT, ENFORCED BY THE TYPE-MAP BUILD AND BY CONFORMANCE CLASS 11 RATHER THAN HERE: 'more specific precedes more general' requires deciding whether one path pattern subsumes another, which no JSON Schema keyword can do, so a map whose general entry is listed first compiles clean and shadows the specific one. That shadowing is silent and it changes the tag, which changes the root, so the build MUST report it. uniqueItems is deliberately NOT set: first-match-wins already gives a duplicated entry a defined meaning, and uniqueItems would catch only wholly identical entries while leaving the case that actually matters - two entries with the same pattern and jsonKind but different tags - untouched, which is a half-measure of exactly the kind this file avoids elsewhere.

pattern.description: Path pattern in display notation, where '*' matches any single array index and '**' matches any run of segments. Example: 'fhirBundle.entry[*].resource.valueQuantity.value'. The pattern addresses the STRUCTURED path (spec section 5); the display form is used here only because it is readable, and an implementation MUST match against decoded segments rather than against a rendered string. STATED LIMIT: minLength is all this schema constrains, and that is deliberate rather than an omission. No grammar for this display notation is pinned by ROAX-CANON/1, so a pattern here would be inventing one in a schema instead of in the specification, and the type map does not exist yet (spec section 4.3). Pinning the grammar belongs with building the map; until then the type-map build owns the check. Note also that spec section 5.2 forbids reasoning over display paths, so this field is the one place a display string is authored on purpose, and the matching still happens on decoded segments.

jsonKind.description: Restricts this entry to a particular observed JSON kind at that path. Present because polymorphic fields are real and already in the reference records: in the shipped vaccination sample, fhirBundle.entry[0].identifier[0].type is the string "PPN" while identifier[1].type is the object { text: "NRIC" }. A map keyed by path alone cannot express that (spec section 4.2). Omit when the path is monomorphic.

tag.description: ROAX type tag: 0 NULL, 1 BOOL, 2 STRING, 3 INTEGER, 4 DECIMAL, 5 BYTES, 6 EMPTY_ARRAY, 7 EMPTY_OBJECT, 8 BLOB_REF. Tags 6 and 7 are produced by the flattener for empty containers and are not normally asserted here. Tag 8 selects the content-addressed blob binding, which is REGISTERED and selected by NO version-1 profile: an implementation MUST reject a type map that binds any path to tag 8 until a profile document under docs/profiles/ declares the binding for that path, and that profile MUST also state how the blob is carried out of band (spec section 6.5). It is accepted by this schema for the same reason Poseidon-BN254 is accepted in the envelope's hashAlg enum - so that the form is pinned once now rather than retrofitted after five independent implementations exist, which is the change that splits a library family.

source.description: Where this binding came from, so a reviewer can check it. E.g. the FHIR element declaration that says this element is `decimal`.

$comment: Unknown paths MUST fail closed (spec section 4.2). DECISION D7 IS RULED D7a, permanently, on 2026-07-28. This schema deliberately provides no default-tag or fallback field, and adding one is now a violation rather than a pending question: a type map that could express 'anything else is a STRING' would let two libraries with different maps silently agree on a wrong root, which is the exact failure this project exists to remove. The pressure to add it will arrive from a real issuer with a real record that a PDT type map has not yet been extended to cover, because the PDT base object permits additional properties (docs/profiles/pdt-healthcert.md section 5); the answer is to extend the map and bump typeMapVersion. THAT EXTENSION MUST BE ADDITIVE. An entry that retags a path the map already covers changes the root of every already-issued record reaching that path, which spec section 12.2 forbids.
